The first 20 minutes of the match were fiercely contested. After a "hydration break," each side saw a player booked — England's midfielder Elliot Anderson and Argentina's centre-back Lisandro Martínez. Towards the end of the first half, almost every whistle was greeted with cheers from the home fans, while opposition fouls drew boos.

The two teams went into the break evenly matched, but after switching ends for the second half, England's Anthony Gordon broke the deadlock in the 55th minute, putting England 1-0 up and sending the England supporters into raptures.

Trailing by a goal, Argentina mounted a fierce comeback. Within 10 minutes, they launched three attacks down the right flank, but all were repelled, drawing sighs from the Argentine fans. Not until the 85th minute did Enzo Fernández head in a cross from Messi to level the score at 1-1, sparking wild celebrations among Argentine supporters — drums pounding, horns blowing — in a fervent atmosphere.

In stoppage time, in the 92nd minute, Messi provided an assist and Lautaro Martínez struck the decisive blow to defeat England, leading Argentina into the final where they will face Spain for the World Cup trophy. Argentine fans in attendance erupted once more; the moment the final whistle blew, they embraced in frenzied celebration, with some even waving cardboard cutouts of Messi purchased from a shopping mall.

Argentine fan Ho, who said he had supported Messi since the latter's emergence at Barcelona, was wearing Argentina's "two-star" number 10 jersey. He noted that this tournament would be Messi's last World Cup and that the team was also looking to defend its title. Although Messi and the team have been surrounded by controversy this tournament, Ho believed that rather than getting bogged down in refereeing decisions in every match, fans should cherish Messi's remaining appearances in the national team shirt. He joked that, while he was still young enough to endure it, he had chosen to stay up all night at the mall to watch the game.

England fans have been singing "Football's coming home!" throughout the tournament, but this time their wish did not come true. Declan, who is studying in the UK and returned to Hong Kong for the summer holiday, draped himself in the England flag alongside his friends today, cheering the team on with all his might. He said it was his first time watching a match at a shopping mall to soak up the atmosphere, and felt that although the fans were passionate, they respected one another, with no serious clashes breaking out.

Disappointment is inevitable when the team you support loses. Declan — who shares his name with England midfielder Declan Rice — felt that England had performed well in this match. A fan of two World Cups, he said plainly: "We've waited 60 years — waiting another four years is nothing!"

Argentina will face Spain on the 20th in their bid to defend the title, while the third-place playoff will see England take on France on the 19th.
